item.title: Five Plays: North Carolina First Quarter
item.description: I thought it was really great that they got an early shot down the field to Lawayne McCoy as he returned from his injury. He and Lincoln Keinholz have a unique connection, so getting that back on track was important for the offense. It was a small thing in the overall context of the game, […]
item.content:encoded:
I thought it was really great that they got an early shot down the field to Lawayne McCoy as he returned from his injury. He and Lincoln Keinholz have a unique connection, so getting that back on track was important for the offense. It was a small thing in the overall context of the game, but setting a tone that you can spread the field will change the way the defense calls the game.

I also just love the way that McCoy uses the field to his advantage as an outside receiver. It starts with his split on this play. He lines up inside the numbers to give himself plenty of room from the sideline. Then, he releases towards the cornerback with a slight shade to the outside before he breaks outside towards the sideline. Finally, he gets a little bit of a stack on the corner, where he gets beyond him to the point that the corner would have to go through him to get to the ball. A lot of subtle stuff here, but it combines to make this a very easy chunk play.

As I’ve pointed out before, I am not in the huddle or the meeting rooms to know exactly what should happen on a play. With that being said, I’m fairly certain that Linc makes the wrong throw here. His read should be the #15 on this play, or whichever defender flows with Isaac Brown’s motion. Since no one reacts to Brown, he should be throwing this to the flat to let Brown make a play.

I think he predetermines his decision on this play and wants to hit the receiver who will be right at the first-down marker. I can’t blame him for assuming the linebacker would follow Brown into the flat. That’s what he should be doing. At least someone on the defense should be chasing the best player on the field into a wide-open space. But Keinholz needs to get into his motion more quickly on this play so that he has a beat of time to assess the defense. By the time he turns his hips, he has to let this rip to be on time with his throw.

If you regularly read this series, you know I rarely mention refs. But what are we doing here? Clev Lubin gets tackled by the center on this play while being pulled to the ground by the left guard. I’ll give you the guard as Clev is falling into him, but this is a form tackle by the center. He could play defensive line with this effort.

He may get home and get a sack or force a poor throw if he’s not held on this play. A flag likely leads to a three-and-out. Instead, UNC continues the drive and ends up with a touchdown. I will say this: I loved this look from the defense. They shifted before the snap and adjusted to the motion to rebalance themselves. Lubin’s rush works, in part, because the interior offensive linemen are forced to zone-block because they don’t know who is going to rush. He takes advantage with a bull rush that nearly works.

This was one of the better games from the offensive line, which was really good to see, as they continue to stack good performances. UNC is solid up front, and they do a good job of getting penetration. They were not able to do that in this game because the line did a good job of staying connected and getting push.

Johnnie Brown and Eryx Daugherty stand out on this play, with Brown getting out to the edge player with good quickness to clear out the path of the run. Daughtery makes a really impressive effort to get inside the defensive tackle who is well to the right of him. He gets to his reach block, and I really love seeing his awareness on this play. After he gets his shoulder underneath the defender to cut him off from the play, he realizes Isaac isn’t past him yet, so he quickly turns back to ensure the defender can’t get back into the play.

Throw in Evan Wibberley’s outstanding climb to the linebacker to take out him out of the play, and you get exactly what you need from the line. They do just enough to let Isaac work. He ends up getting six or so more yards on his own on this play.

Another very good job blocking by the offensive line on this play. Wibberley goes to battle with the nose guard on this play, which is the next best thing when you don’t get push. Create a stalemate so that you give your back a chance. I can’t stress how much better this is than allowing penetration. Brown and Daugherty do a great job of completing their blocks again, and Isaac has a clean lane to run through. He’s an ankle tackle away from an easy touchdown here, and the line deserves the credit for that.

You can’t possibly imagine how much I wanted this play to go for a touchdown. I’m chalking it up to a really good play by the UNC secondary players. The safeties and the corner to the top of the screen hold their water before they flow to the ball. The middle linebacker does the same. Cason Henry is half a step away from getting a better connection on his block, but he does enough to give Linc a cutback opportunity. Unfortunately, the safeties are right there to make a play. Still love the design of this play.

item.title: 2027 NFL Mock Draft: Eagles 7-round simulation, Version 1.0
item.description: ﻿How would you grade this projection?
item.content:encoded:
The 2026 Philadelphia Eagles season is all but over and the most exciting thing for the team is the future. Now rich with draft picks in the 2027 and 2028 drafts, the Birds are entering a rebuilding period after a four-year stretch of being one of the league’s best teams. There are many questions regarding the coaching staff and quarterback, but there’s no question the Eagles need to get younger and more athletic at practically every position. It’s early, and much will change about the Eagles 2027 NFL Draft outlook, but here is a picture of what it could look like right now with their projected 10 draft picks. 

Using the PFF Mock Draft Simulator with their draft board and not making any trades.

1.05: Jeremiah Smith, Wide Receiver, Ohio State: Jeremiah Smith is the best receiver prospect to come out of college since Julio Jones and AJ Green. Getting him with the fifth overall pick would be a coup. He would enter the league as a top 10 receiver and make a formidable pass catching corps with DeVonta Smith and Makai Lemon. 

1.26: CJ Carr, Quarterback, Notre Dame: It’s very hard to envision a scenario where Jalen Hurts comes back to Philadelphia. It’s not impossible, but it feels highly unlikely given a multitude of factors. If he leaves, the Eagles will look to a deep quarterback class to hit the reset button. CJ Carr doesn’t have the most experience, but he has all the tools to be a high level passer in the NFL. He is smart with a big arm and good mobility. He will need patience in development, but his upside is very high. 

2.37: Carter Smith, Offensive Tackle, Indiana: The Eagles have needs everywhere, and the offensive line is high on the priority list. Carter Smith is a highly experienced blocker who could take over day one at right tackle next year as the Eagles try to fill Lane Johnson’s shoes. 

3.97: Sahir West, Edge Defender, UCLA: Sahir West is a bit of a tweener who has played all over the UCLA defensive line, dominating wherever he lines up. In the NFL, he may benefit from dropping some weight and becoming a true edge player where his motor and first step could make him a dangerous presence on rebuilding defense. 

4.104: Zabien Brown, Cornerback, Alabama: Riq Woolen is a free agent after this season. The Eagles need another perimeter cornerback. Zabien Brown might not be a day one starter, but he has the athleticism to eventually compete for snaps on the outside. 

5.142: Nate Frazier, Running Back, Georgia: The Eagles will need to prepare for a post-Saquon Barkley era. Age and injuries have caught up to the lead back and Philly will need to rejuvenate their offensive backfield this spring. Nate Frazier is an easy evaluation with his strong running style and great burst. He’s not a game changing back, but he can be a chain mover in the right offense. 

5.150: Eli Finley, Tight End, Louisiana Tech: It’s unclear if Eli Stowers will be the guy the Eagles wanted. I hope he does, but the team still clearly needs some more tight end depth anyway. Eli Finley is a great receiving tight end who can really give them some quality youth at the position. 

5.153: Tobi Osunsanmi, Edge Defender, Indiana: Tobi Osunsanmi is one of the biggest breakout players in the country this season. After years at Kansas State, Osunsanmi has emerged as one of the best pass rushers in college football. His track background combines with a hellacious motor to make him tough to block at the FBS level. Do his athletic tools translate? He would be a great day three flier. 

7.224: Rod Moore Junior, Safety, Michigan: Rod Moore is a rangy, albeit undersized safety on the back end of the Michigan defense. He has some great coverage skills, but leaves some to be desired as a run defender. The Eagles safety situation right now is not great and some swings on high upside athletes makes a lot of sense. 

7.238: Griffin Wilde, Wide Receiver, Northwestern: Griffin Wilde really strikes me as a player who will outplay his draft position. He is hidden away on an unconventional Northwestern offense, but he does big things every week for the Wildcats. He is big bodied, athletic, and sure handed. He could immediately push for snaps on an Eagles team in desperate need of pass catchers.

item.title: NFL news, live updates: Aidan Hutchinson reportedly suffers torn ACL on sack celebration; Patriots QB Drake Maye out indefinitely with ankle injury
item.description: Follow along with the latest NFL news coming out of Week 10.
item.content:encoded:
Another NFL Sunday is in the books, with just one game left in Week 10 as the Baltimore Ravens host the LA Chargers on "Monday Night Football."

Sunday kicked off with a bang as the Detroit Lions and New England Patriots faced off in Munich, Germany, with injuries to two stars that will have all eyes drawn as the new week plays out. Lions star defensive end Aidan Hutchinson suffered what is feared to be a season-ending ACL tear while celebrating a sack against Patriots quarterback Drake Maye … who suffered an ankle injury on that very sack, which knocked him out of the game and could cost him the season.

Week 10 also offered us our first look at Las Vegas Raiders No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza as a starter. He led scoring drives on each of the Raiders' first two possessions and entered halftime with a 10-7 lead over the Seattle Seahawks, but Drew Lock rallied with two passing touchdowns in the third quarter to take the lead, improving to 3-0 as a starter for Seattle this season. Raiders star tight end Brock Bowers exited the loss with an ankle injury.

item.title: Steelers WR Roman Wilson trending towards playing vs. Eagles
item.description: It looks like the Steelers will get a boost to their WR room this weekend against the Eagles.
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers may finally be getting one of their to receivers back in the lineup in Week 11.

Mark Kaboly of the Pat McAfee Show reported on Tuesday morning that wide receiver Roman Wilson is trending toward coming off injured reserve and playing in Week 11 as the team travels to Philadelphia to take on the Eagles.

Yesterday in his weekly press conference, Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy said he was “hopeful” to have both Wilson and Michael Pittman Jr. back this week to help bolster the receiver room. At least one of them is now likely to return this week. Wilson has been on injured reserve since Week 5 after suffering a finger injury against the Indianapolis Colts.

The 84th pick in the 2024 NFL Draft has already posted a career high in receiving yards this season with 188 in five games played. Wilson had emerged as a downfield threat for Rodgers and one of the Steelers’ best man coverage beaters before his injury. Wilson’s return should provide a boost to the Steelers’ passing game that has been lackluster for several weeks now.

The Steelers have yet to open the 21-day practice window for the receiver, which they would then have to activate him for him to be eligible to play this Sunday. With the team not practicing on Tuesdays, Wednesday should give us a clearer view of the team’s plans for the receiver this weekend.

item.title: Week 11 fantasy tight end rankings: Top TE streamers, starts
item.description: The Colts' Tyler Warren was the TE4 last season as a rookie, but he's fallen off the fantasy map in 2026. Can he rebound this week at Houston?
item.content:encoded:
One of the great mysteries of this fantasy football season is what happened to Indianapolis Colts tight end Tyler Warren.

Last year's TE4 as a rookie, Warren was expected to be an elite option at the position in 2026. But it just hasn't happened. And in fact, he seems to have regressed.

With the Colts trading away wideouts Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the deadline, Warren appeared poised to cash in … but in his first game post-deadline, he managed just two receptions for 1 yard against the Dolphins.

A one-week anomaly? Or the new norm? We have Warren ranked as TE11 this week.

item.title: CB Nazeeh Johnson visited the Steelers Tuesday
item.description: Cornerback Nazeeh Johnson is trying to find a way back into the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Cornerback Nazeeh Johnson is trying to find a way back into the NFL.

According to multiple reports, Johnson visited with the Steelers on Tuesday.

Johnson signed with the Titans in July, but hurt his ankle and was placed on injured reserve in August. He was released off that list later in the month and then served a six-game suspension for violating the performance-enhancing drug policy to open the season.

Johnson was a Chiefs seventh-round pick in 2022 and he played 29 games while with Kansas City. He had 66 tackles, three tackles for loss, a sack and three passes defensed in those appearances.

item.description: Yahoo Fantasy is teaming up with BreakingT to celebrate the player that defined the fantasy week.
item.content:encoded:
Yahoo Fantasy is teaming up withBreakingT, home of the fastest-licensed fan gear in the world, to launch the Yahoo Fantasy Shirt of the Week, celebrating the one play or player that defined the fantasy week. The names on your roster are about to be the names on your chest.

BreakingT is a newsroom that happens to make shirts. Using its proprietary CrowdBreak platform, BreakingT tracks what fans are reacting to across social media in real time — surfacing the moments, memes and micro-stories that matter most to each fanbase — and its design team turns those moments into officially licensed gear in hours, not months.

item.title: NFL Week 11 betting: 5 biggest storylines, including favorites dominating and some huge point spreads
item.description: For the second straight week, favorites were on fire.
item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Chargers are on the board.

The Chargers weren't just the last NFL team to win a game this season; they were the last team that had not covered the spread. They checked off both boxes on Monday night by beating the Ravens as 4.5-point underdogs. The Chargers and the Philadelphia Eagles are the only teams that have covered the spread just once this season.

Here are the biggest betting storylines for Week 11 of the NFL season:

Favorites rule again

The NFL season became chalky all of a sudden.

For the second straight week, favorites dominated. In Week 9 favorites were 14-1 straight up and 11-3-1 against the spread. Then in Week 10 it almost repeated, with favorites going 10-3 straight up and 9-4 against the spread going into Monday night's game. The Chargers scored one for the underdogs on Monday night with a win over the Ravens.

Part of the reason for the favorites suddenly dominating is there are more than a few teams that are helplessly out of the playoff race already. We saw that at the trade deadline. The contenders got stronger, with many first- and second-round picks being moved for players. That also meant the also-rans got worse.

Oddsmakers will adjust spreads. We can see that a bit in some huge Week 11 spreads. But we're likely to see the gap between the best and worst teams widen. We'll see if the point spreads keep up with that trend.

Big spreads in Week 11

Anyone still alive in a survival pool will have multiple options to choose from in Week 11.

There are five double-digit favorites in Week 11. There are the two biggest spreads of the NFL season included in that group. The Chiefs are 16-point favorites over the Cardinals, who are quarterbacked by rookie Carson Beck. The Bills are 16.5-point favorites over the Dolphins, who are quarterbacked by Kyle McCord.

It's projected to be a lopsided week in the NFL, though that's often when we see chaos.

Joe Burrow the new MVP favorite

With another big game on Sunday night, Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow took over as the clear favorite in the NFL MVP race.

Burrow is -115 to win MVP, with Josh Allen now trailing at +350. The other big change is that Jordan Love went from the top five of the odds to +6000, making it a four-man race, according to oddsmakers.

Burrow has been on fire and his next two games are against the Commanders and Saints, who don't have great defenses.

Offense vs. defense on Sunday night

We get a fantastic matchup for Sunday night in Week 11. It's a showdown between a 49ers team leading the NFL in offensive EPA (expected points added) and the Vikings, who lead the NFL in defensive EPA. Oddsmakers prefer the 49ers, who are at home. They're 3-point favorites, and even -3.5 at some sportsbooks.

The 49ers have had a remarkable season, and the Vikings looked rejuvenated with Kirk Cousins taking over at quarterback in Week 10. It could be a playoff preview on Sunday night.

Oddsmakers not worried about Lions

The Lions lost defensive end Aidan Hutchinson to a torn ACL on Sunday. They were already without linebacker Jack Campbell. Even though the Lions are without their two best defensive players, the betting market doesn't think there will be a big drop.

The Lions are 6.5-point favorites in Week 11 over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who are coming off a bye. And they are strong favorites to still make the playoffs in a crowded NFC wild-card race. The odds for the Lions to make the playoffs at BetMGM are -525. The odds on them missing the playoffs are +400. Apparently the betting market believes the Lions can continue to outscore everyone.

item.title: NFL playoff picture entering Week 11: Lions pacing NFC North, even after Aidan Hutchinson injury, Kirk Cousins trade
item.description: Detroit sat in the seventh slot just a month ago. Its improved standing doesn't reflect the team's current vibes. Meanwhile, the Vikings find themselves as the No. 5 seed. Yet, now that they have Kirk Cousins, it feels like their potential is greater.
item.content:encoded:
When we last looked at the potential playoff field a month ago, the Minnesota Vikings sat in the No. 2 hole — and we had our share of questions about them.

Now the Vikings find themselves as the No. 5 seed in the projected playoff field, if the regular season ended today. Thankfully for Minnesota it does not. And yet, now that it has Kirk Cousins at quarterback, it feels like its potential is greater than ever this season.

On the flip side, the Detroit Lions sat in the seventh slot just a month ago. They're now on a five-game winning streak and have zoomed up to the No. 2 seed.

Hooray?

That part isn't the bad news, but Aidan Hutchinson's injury is, and it's hard to imagine Detroit not feeling the effects of it in a significant way, especially with the other three NFC North teams all currently in the playoff field.

There's also one more thing you'll notice: Both Super Bowl teams from last season are currently the first teams out in their respective conferences. The Seattle Seahawks still have the means to crash the postseason party again, but the New England Patriots are going to have a whale of a time getting back after Drake Maye's ankle injury.

Here's how the seeding would line up if the playoffs started today:

AFC

1. Bills (8-1)

The Bills have quietly won five straight, with the last three all by 17 points or more, including dominating the pre-Kirk Vikings in Minnesota. Fans might have wanted more fireworks at the trade deadline, but Amani Hooker jumped right into a starting role and appeared to elevate the secondary, even with a concerning Christian Benford injury complicating matters. They'll have one more tuneup game (Miami) before the meat of the schedule hits, starting with the Thanksgiving game vs. Kansas City. We know what's at stake in that one. Josh Allen has continued to offset some of this team's shortcomings, but this feels like a better Bills operation than a year ago. 

2. Chiefs (7-2)

Kenneth Walker III had arguably been the Chiefs' most valuable player prior to Week 10, and without him Sunday they scored 35 points and had one of their more complete offensive performances, with rookie Emmett Johnson leading the way. Josh Downs also had an auspicious debut, giving the Chiefs one of their most balanced attacks in the passing game they've had in a few years. They've also ironed some things out defensively. If the Chiefs can avoid a Seahawks-style offensive crashout, they can stay atop the AFC West, although the Broncos are right on their heels, also at 7-2 after those teams split the two regular-season meetings.

3. Jaguars (7-2)

You can make a case for the Jaguars being one of the more complete teams in football, especially after the trade-deadline week acquisitions of Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux. The Jags played Godchaux 17 snaps against the Titans in Week 10 and rested their other two additions on defense and still won by 17. The AFC South is nearly locked up, with the rest of the division at 3-6 or worse. The Jaguars have their sights set even higher. They're gunning for the AFC's top seed and are gearing up for a Super Bowl run. The tests will come away from home: Four of their next six games will be on the road against teams still reasonably in the playoff mix, starting Sunday against the Giants.

4. Bengals (7-2)

The Bengals are very much back in the thick of the race, thanks to four straight victories, and Joe Burrow has to be among the handful of MVP favorites, with 20 TD passes in his past five games. If the Bengals can sweep the Browns, the division might just run through Cincinnati. The schedule isn't daunting, but there's a terrific test against the Chiefs upcoming that will give us an idea just how good the Bengals are. This might not be the most balanced team out there, but the Bengals certainly qualify as dangerous with a hot Burrow and those wide receivers coming at you.  

5. Broncos (7-2)

Coming out of the bye, the Broncos are very much on a playoff track, but as the first wild-card team, they're doing whatever they can to overtake the Chiefs for the West crown. The schedule lays out nicely for the Broncos overall, even with a few tough holiday games (Steelers on Black Friday, Bills on Christmas) staring them down. The Broncos instill some doubt because of all their close-game victories, and it has been a two-year pattern. If Bo Nix can level up and Denver's defense can tackle better and limit explosive plays, the Broncos are capable of beating almost anyone. They've handled a tougher schedule well to this point. 

6. Steelers (6-3)

The blowout loss to the Bengals on Sunday night undercut some of what they accomplished, dropping them from first place in the AFC North to back in a hunting position. Does Aaron Rodgers have enough in the tank to get the passing game going? The Bengals showed how vulnerable the Steelers can be when Jaylen Warren is contained. Pittsburgh's defense also looked helpless to stop a dominant passing attack, which was concerning. The Steelers can finish with 11 or more wins against a fairly manageable remaining schedule, and a wild-card spot feels more than likely, but does this team have any upward mobility beyond that?

7. Browns (6-4)

This year's darlings are still hanging onto a playoff spot, benefiting from their comeback victory over the Texans and losses from the Patriots and Ravens. There's a pathway to the postseason in Todd Monken's first season, and he deserves Coach of the Year attention. The Browns are by no means a perfect operation, but they are young and hungry and can still snag the AFC North (something not done in Cleveland since the 1989 season) with a sweep of the Bengals the most likely way of achieving that. Browns fans might still be holding their noses a bit with Deshaun Watson at quarterback, but to his credit, he's delivered some big moments this season.

NFC

1. 49ers (8-1)

Sunday's win over Dallas was a reminder of this team's potential vulnerability of getting caught in a shootout. It wasn't a problem against the Cowboys and Cardinals, but the Falcons loss lingers. Still, this team can punch with the best of them, injuries or not, and tough schedule or not, the Niners are going to be in it until the end. Holding off the Rams and Seahawks won't be a given, even as those teams have underachieved and have lost at home to the Niners in the first meetings. Brock Purdy is a deserving MVP candidate, and with a healthy Mike Evans and decent health down the stretch, this team can win it all. The Week 11 game in Mexico City against the Vikings is a potential NFC championship game preview.

2. Lions (7-2)

Do you want the good news or bad news first? The good: The Lions sit in the No. 2 hole, atop the best division in football after a five-game win streak. The bad: The Aidan Hutchinson injury is a potential season-wrecker, especially for a defense that had made strides in the weeks leading up to Sunday. The Lions were in a similar situation when Hutch went down two seasons ago, and they held on for the division and the No. 1 seed before being shocked in the playoff loss against the Commanders. This Lions team might not have the same firepower and still must face the Bears twice and Vikings once (in Minneapolis). The playoffs remain a strong possibility, but holding onto the division is going to be a battle.

3. Giants (5-3-1)

To lose their starting quarterback and be in this position is remarkable, but the Giants also have to avoid losses like Thursday's against the Commanders if they want to hold the division. That's two games they should have won against Washington but instead are 0-1-1. J.J. McCarthy deserves credit for the job he's done after the September trade from Minnesota, and we'd love to see a playoff matchup vs. his former team for dramatic storyline purposes, but the Giants don't have this division wrapped up yet by any means. A tough schedule lies ahead, and the Commanders and Cowboys remain within striking distance.

4. Panthers (4-5)

Carolina's underachieving defense and an inconsistent Bryce Young are holding this team back. A home win over the Ravens on Sunday would give the Panthers two straight victories after the three-game losing streak, but the biggest hurdle to winning the division — the Panthers' only realistic way into the playoffs — will be in the Week 12 Monday night matchup in Tampa. They were blown out by the Bucs in the first meeting and must show something against their biggest NFC South threats. Tampa Bay has the far easier remaining schedule.   

5. Vikings (7-2)

There's no question that the Vikings' trajectory has changed dramatically after one game with Kirk Cousins back. He wasn't perfect in the Vikings' win at Green Bay, but he was better than Kyler Murray or Carson Wentz was in any of their starts this season. With a defense that's historically good, Minnesota's offense merely needs to be capable, and Cousins was more than that. There are three games that likely will determine this team's seed: Sunday's game against the Niners in Mexico City, the Week 15 Sunday nighter against the Lions and the Week 18 showdown against the Bears. Both divisional matchups are in Minnesota, and they each could be classics. 

6. Bears (7-2)

If the No. 5-seed Vikings are dangerous, what are the No. 6-seed Bears? They've won four straight with Caleb Williams back in the lineup, and the bye week figured to help the healing of Kyle Monangai and Luther Burden III, both important players to keep in the lineup. The Bears have displayed Super Bowl potential at their best this season, but navigating the final stretch will be daunting. Even with Miami and New Orleans on the schedule, Chicago's remaining opponents are probably the toughest of any team still in the mix. The Jeffery Simmons trade has energized this defense, and Williams is as scary as any QB out there, but the Bears have their work cut out for them to secure solid playoff footing. 

7. Packers (6-4)

Following a six-game stretch where the Packers played just about as well as anyone in the league, they were dealt a humbling home loss to the Vikings on Sunday. The defeat gave Minnesota the season sweep in a division where every tiebreaker matters. That, along with the 1-2 hole Green Bay dug for itself, has pushed the Packers down to the playoff basement for now. They're chasing every other NFC North team, and the Seahawks and Rams are nipping at their heels with matching 6-4 records. With games left against the Rams, Bills, Bears and Lions, there's little margin for error. The possible Week 12 return of Micah Parsons gives Green Bay a potential ace in the hole.

item.title: Packers-Rams Thanksgiving Eve game gets iconic halftime act
item.description: Legendary band U2 will headline the halftime show of the NFL’s new Thanksgiving Eve game
item.content:encoded:
The NFL’s march towards global domination takes another step this year with the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game, featuring the Green Bay Packers versus the Los Angeles Rams on the Wednesday night before the Thanksgiving holiday in the United States.

And the league is bringing one of the biggest rock bands in history with them.

Netflix announced on Tuesday that U2 will perform at halftime of the Thanksgiving Eve game between the Packers and the Rams, promoting the appearance from the “iconic band” on social media, complete with a voiceover from Matthew McConaughey:

U2 has been featured during halftime of an NFL game before, most notably during Super Bowl XXXVI. That performance came months after the September 11 attacks, and the band played three songs: “Beautiful Day,” “MLK,” and “Where the Streets Have No Name.”

During the final song, a scrolling list of names of those who lost their lives on 9/11 was featured, ending with lead singer Bono opening his jacket to reveal an American flag lining.

Of course, others may be most familiar with U2 when the band’s album Songs of Innocence was automatically pushed to users of Apple devices back in 2014. The backlash to that decision led to Apple releasing a removal tool, and Bono apologizing for the rollout.

Still, “Every Breaking Wave” was a solid song, if you ask me.

item.title: Chargers' win puts Titans in the driver's seat for the first pick in the 2027 NFL draft
item.description: There are no winless teams in the NFL after the Chargers won on Monday night.
item.content:encoded:
There are no winless teams in the NFL after the Chargers won on Monday night. Which might be good news for the Titans.

There's now a three-way tie for the worst record in the NFL, with the Titans, Chargers and Dolphins all at 1-8. The draft order tiebreaker goes to the team with the weakest strength of schedule, and that gives the Titans an edge.

The Titans' 17 opponents this season currently have a cumulative winning percentage of .481, which gives them a big edge over the Chargers (whose strength of schedule is.528) and Dolphins (.588). The Titans also have a weaker strength of schedule than the 2-8 Jets and 2-7 Eagles, who are next in the draft order. If there's a tie for the first pick, the Titans are likely to win it.

If the Titans end up with the first overall pick, the big question will be whether they believe in quarterback Cam Ward enough to use the first pick to build around him, or whether they think it's time to draft a quarterback to replace Ward. The current betting favorite to be the first overall pick is Ohio State wide receiver Jeremiah Smith. Drafting Smith would be a strong statement that the Titans are committed to putting the right players around Ward. After the Chargers' loss on Monday, the Titans are in good shape to get that opportunity.

item.title: NFL power rankings: Despite dominating win, Lions fall following Hutchinson injury
item.description: A look at where the Detroit Lions sit in the the NFL’s 2026 Week 11 power rankings.
item.content:encoded:
The Detroit Lions (7-2) are riding a five-game win streak and are coming off a dominating 35-10 win over the New England Patriots in Germany. Their offense is firing on all cylinders, their defense is improving (they’ve allowed just 12.8 points against per game over the last four games), and they currently sit atop the NFC North because they’re 2-0 in divisional games, ahead of the Vikings (7-2, 3-1 in division), Bears (7-2, 0-2), and Packers (6-4, 1-3).

While the Lions have been on an upward trajectory for over a month, they lost star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson for the season in their last game, and the national media seems convinced it will be the Lions’ undoing.

Of the eight national power rankings we track, the Lions fell in five, stayed level in two, and climbed in just one. When comparing the Lions’ ranking to those within the division, the Lions land at third in all but one ranking, with the Bears ahead on every list and the Vikings ahead on all but CBS Sports, despite the Lions holding a head-to-head victory over them just three games ago.

So while the national pundits are dropping the Lions down their rankings and worrying over what could have been or where things go from here, Lions coach Dan Campbell refuses to discount this team despite their injury obstacles:

Let’s take a closer look at this week’s national power rankings.

NFL.com: 8 (Previous rank: 7)

From Nick Shook:

Detroit’s offense is among the most consistent units in the NFL — save for Week 9 — and the team continues to enjoy improvement from the defensive side. The Lions only fall this week because of movement around them, although I am quite concerned with how they’re going to replace Aidan Hutchinson’s production.

CBS Sports: 8 (Previous rank: 8)

From Pete Prisco:

The loss of Aidan Hutchinson with a knee injury could be a damning blow to this defense. The high-powered offense might need to score even more.

Sporting News: 8 (Previous rank: 10)

From Vinnie Iyer:

The Lions are up to a five-game winning streak after starting 2-2. Amon-Ra St. Brown’s monster game in Munich reminds that Jared Goff has fully embraced an aggressive wide receiver-centric offense. The simplicity of the production has them flying under the radar a little to other NFC contenders.

Sports Illustrated: 9 (Previous rank: 6)

From Connor Orr:

I hate to knock the Lions down after a convincing win over the Patriots, but losing Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson may be a bridge too far for this team to recover from. I think the Lions are still good enough to limp into the playoffs, but can this offense score at a historic rate to make up for all the attrition?

The Athletic: 9 (Previous rank: 8)

From Chad Graff and Josh Kendall:

Breakout player: Alim McNeill

The sixth-year defensive tackle already has a career high in sacks (6.5) and quarterback hits (11), and the Lions are going to need him more than ever with Aidan Hutchinson out due to injury. Detroit proved again Sunday that its offense is Super Bowl-worthy, but the defense is 28th in the league in defensive EPA (minus-5.2 per 100 snaps).

USA Today: 10 (Previous rank: 6)

From Nate Davis:

Barring another catastrophic injury, hard to envision a scenario where this team misses the playoffs. But it might be wise to begin conserving RB Jahmyr Gibbs’ touches, because he may need 30 per game in January if this team is going to make any kind of Super Bowl push.

ESPN: 10 (Previous rank: 10)

From ESPN Staff, excerpt from Eric Woodyard:

Non-QB MVP at midseason: RB Jahmyr Gibbs

There’s a reason the Lions made Gibbs the NFL’s highest-paid running back over the offseason. And he has proved to be worth every penny after a phenomenal start to his fourth season as the team’s clear lead back. With 62 career touchdowns, the 24-year-old recently passed Hall of Famer Terrell Davis (61) for the most through a player’s first four seasons in NFL history, per ESPN Research. His 1,384 scrimmage yards are the most a Lions player has produced through the first nine games of any season, and he has already scored 13 touchdowns. 

Yahoo Sports: 11 (Previous rank: 9)

From Frank Schwab:

The Lions’ season changed with the reported ACL injury to defensive end Aidan Hutchinson. They were already without linebacker Jack Campbell, arguably the second-best player on the defense, and Detroit lost its unquestioned star because of a sack celebration. That’s brutal. Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum are capable vets and will fill in, but they’re nowhere near Hutchinson’s level.

“Any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy,” Lions head coach Dan Campbell said, according to NFL.com.

The Lions won on Sunday without Hutchinson for most of the game to improve to 7-2, and perhaps they have enough wins banked to make the playoffs in what will be a difficult wild-card race. But their hopes of being a Super Bowl contender are likely dashed without their two best defensive players.

item.title: Jerry Jones says Cowboys evaluating DC Christian Parker's future
item.description: Changes may be coming for Dallas Cowboys defensive coordinator Christian Parker, according to team owner Jerry Jones.
item.content:encoded:
Could the Dallas Cowboys be planning to make a change at defensive coordinator?

The Cowboys' sixth loss of the season on Sunday, Nov. 15, emphasized that defense is still the team's biggest weakness. Jerry Jones, team owner, president and general manager, said on Tuesday, Nov. 17, that the Cowboys are discussing current DC Christian Parker's future.

Jones joined Dallas-Fort Worth sports radio station 105.3 The FAN, where he was asked if the team would be changing Parker's role or responsibilities.

"We're talking about that, but I’m not going to talk about that here. But we are talking about those things," Jones said.

JERRY JONES: Cowboys historic defensive struggle vs. 49ers 'glaring'

Jerry Jones on @1053SS, @rjchoppy and @BobbyBeltTX on Christian Parker's future: "We're talking about that, but I’m not going to talk about that here. But we are talking about those things.” https://t.co/Ovoh1IUXSl

— 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) November 17, 2026

Jones also noted that any changes the Cowboys are considering may happen as soon as this week. Before making the decision, the team is also considering how any move could impact the rest of the season.

Jones also drew a comparison to Sean Payton, who had his play-calling duties taken away by the Giants in 2002. When the Cowboys hired him in 2003, they gave him a chance to call plays again, Jones said. He mentioned that play-calling changes can happen in-season or on a week-by-week basis, and he pointed out that many play-callers have given up their duties when things have gone poorly.

"Bottom line is – to be trite – we've got a lot of room for improvement," Jones said.

In Week 10, Dallas had a chance to tighten the gap on the Giants' NFC East lead after New York's third loss of the season. The Cowboys squandered that chance by losing a 46-40 shoot-out to the 49ers on Nov. 15. The 584 yards the Cowboys allowed in the game were the most the team has allowed in a home game in franchise history.

Through 10 games, Dallas has allowed 28.2 points per outing, which is third most in the NFL, and 393.8 yards per game, which is the most in the NFL. Only the 2-7 Eagles and 3-7 Colts have fewer takeaways than the Cowboys' eight so far this year.

"I feel very resigned to trying to figure this out. And I don't think our season is over," Jones' son and Cowboys co-owner Stephen Jones said on Nov. 16. "I think we're making it very difficult on ourselves, and we're digging a big hole that we're going to have to come out of.

"But I do think we have the players. I think we got the pieces in place if we could get the chemistry right and execute."

Christian Parker coaching background

Prior to his hiring, Parker appeared to be one of the top young defensive minds in the NFL. His first job in the NFL was with the Packers in 2019, and he had risen up the ranks to become the Eagles' passing game coordinator and defensive backs coach by 2025.

Dallas hired Parker in the offseason to replace Matt Eberflus, who was fired after the 2025 Cowboys' defense finished as one of the worst units in franchise history.

This year's defense is allowing more yards per game (393.8) than 2025's average of 377, but it's also allowing fewer points – 28.2 to last year's NFL-worst 30.1.

item.title: Who will Chargers draft with first overall pick?
item.description: Coach Jim Harbaugh and the Los Angeles Chargers earned their first win of the season but remain in reach of the No. 1 overall pick in 2027 NFL draft.
item.content:encoded:
Coach Jim Harbaugh and the Los Angeles Chargers earned their first win of the season, defeating the Baltimore Ravens 23-20 on "Monday Night Football" on Nov. 16.

The Chargers improved to 1-8 and no longer hold sole possession of the worst record in the NFL as the Tennessee Titans and Miami Dolphins own the same record.

Several weeks remain in the regular season for a team to separate itself from the pack and stumble into the first overall pick.

Harbaugh and the Chargers continue to play with the intention of turning the season around with their current roster after not making an official move at the trade deadline last week.

The team will have another winnable game this week, hosting the 2-8 New York Jets at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. The Dolphins are also on the Chargers’ schedule for a game on Dec. 27, which could also have draft positioning implications.

If the Chargers finish with the top selection in the draft, there are several options to consider.

More: Chargers' nightmare temporarily ends on MNF, but does it change anything?

Who could the Chargers draft in the first round?

There are several prospects for NFL teams like the Chargers to consider early in the first round of the draft.

While positional need will factor into who Los Angeles could target, it could also be in the franchise's best interest to just take the best player available regardless of position.

Jeremiah Smith, Ohio State, WR

The Chargers need a No. 1 receiver. Considering Smith's success and accomplishments at the college level, he could be the next franchise player for the Chargers.

Dylan Stewart, South Carolina, DE/OLB

Defense could be the aim for Los Angeles, and USA TODAY Sports' Michael Middlehurst-Schwartz has the Chargers picking No. 3 in his latest mock draft. With that pick, he has the Chargers going with South Carolina's Dylan Stewart.

"This move might only be in play if the Chargers part ways with Tuli Tuipulotu, with whom the team couldn't reach agreement on a long-term extension this summer," Middlehurst-Schwartz writes. "Yet Los Angeles will need to confront its precipitous fall from the contending class, and it's not out of the question that the team might balk at his price tag. Stewart's singular explosiveness as an edge rusher could compel teams to look past his on-field blow-ups, and he could take his place as a much-needed cornerstone for the Bolts."

Leonard Moore, Notre Dame, CB

The Chargers offense has struggled this season, but there’s plenty of talent on defense they could consider as well. Moore could be the first defender off the board and can be a lockdown cornerback at the professional level.

Colin Simmons, Texas, Edge

Another defensive option, Simmons could be of interest to L.A. The edge rusher has proven he could be a menace for opposing quarterbacks. He produced 5.5 sacks against Tennessee in September.

Chargers draft darkhorse

The Chargers have not looked like a team ready to move on in many regards, but anything is possible.

Drew Mestemaker, Oklahoma State, QB

The Chargers are unlikely to move on from Justin Herbert even after an abysmal year. However, it might be prudent to draft for the future with a high draft pick that comes after a season that went awry early. Oklahoma State's Mestemaker is the first QB off the board in most mock drafts. Another pick could be the well-regarded CJ Carr from Notre Dame.

The Los Angeles #Chargers are now 1-8 this season.

item.title: Myles Garrett left the Browns, now they have better playoff odds
item.description: The Rams’ playoff odds at ESPN are not very good
item.content:encoded:
Myles Garrett requested a trade from the Cleveland Browns so that he could go somewhere with a chance to win a Super Bowl, and now the Los Angeles Rams have worse playoff odds than his former team. After 10 games and more than halfway into the season, the Rams have 46% playoff odds according to ESPN’s FPI metric.

The Browns have a 59% chance to make the playoffs.

In the NFC, the four division winners would be:

  • 49ers
  • Vikings
  • Buccaneers
  • Giants

New York has worse playoff odds than L.A., but they are in the NFC East so there isn’t any competition. Except for the Cowboys, who are right on the Giants’ tail. That doesn’t help the Rams, however.

The top three NFC teams for wil d card spots would be the Lions, the Bears, and the Seahawks.

L.A. isn’t far behind Seattle, just 49% to 46%. Their playoff fates could be decided in Week 16 and Week 18, when the two teams face each other.

The Rams have the toughest remaining strength of schedule, by some metrics.

However, in the AFC, the Browns are 6-4, which is already more wins than they had in either of the past two seasons. Cleveland beat the Houston Texans on Sunday and their favorable schedule continues after the bye week with a matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders and rookie Fernando Mendoza.

Although the Browns have two games left against the Bengals, Cleveland’s remaining schedule could allow them to win 10 games this season. Pretty ironic for a historically awful team that traded its best player to the Rams — and the best player they got in return, Jared Verse, has zero sacks and isn’t doing much to help.

Perhaps where the Browns went right and the Rams went wrong was not in the trade, but in the draft:

Cleveland drafted receivers KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston, both of whom are having standout first seasons in the NFL. Imagine if the Rams had drafted even one of them.

With Drake Maye out for the rest of the season, the Patriots are unlikely to make the playoffs, opening the door for the Browns, who are currently in the seventh seed in the AFC playoff picture. They are followed by the 5-5 Patriots, then the 4-6 Raiders and Ravens. If Cleveland beats the Raiders and Ravens when they meet later this season, they’re almost guaranteed to make the playoffs.

The Rams are not. They’ll have to beat the Packers when they return from the bye week. Green Bay traded for Micah Parsons at the start of last season and we see where that’s gotten them.

Perhaps not every trade for a edge is something that to rush into.

item.title: 'Madden' is a comedy disguised as a biopic. The joke's on us
item.description: "Madden" doesn't take itself seriously, and neither should you.
item.content:encoded:
"Madden," the long-awaited John Madden biopic, would have been better served if it had promoted itself as a comedy from the beginning.

Nicolas Cage puts on a fat suit and some prosthetics to play the legendary Oakland Raiders coach, groundbreaking NFL color commentator and the man who put his name behind one of the most popular and successful video games of all time. But the suspension of belief achieved when an actor fully embodies and immerses themselves in a role to the point where you forget they're playing a character did not happen in this 110-minute film. You know it's Cage the whole time because his portrayal of Madden came with the acclaimed actor's legendary, unmistakable voice, accent and mannerisms.

The film begins with a few documentary-style solo cutaways that are needlessly interspersed throughout the movie. They feature Madden, Raiders owner and Madden's best friend Al Davis, played more successfully by Christian Bale, and Madden's loving wife Virginia, played well by Kathryn Hahn, who's running out of patience in their marriage. The Raiders are 0-5 in AFC championship games under Madden, and Virginia tells him that if they beat the rival Pittsburgh Steelers, he needs to come home to spend more time with his family. Madden, Davis and the Raiders arrive at the Oakland Coliseum for the game, and so does Shane Gillis for some reason as a late cast addition, playing a superstitious neighbor named Vince McGary who brings chicken feet and other good luck charms to the game.

Madden can't stop thinking about football and diagramming plays, and the film hammers home this point by putting them on screen far too many times. While the game play in the film is mediocre, the old-timey yellow score graphics were a nice touch as the movie quickly speeds through the Raiders' two wins over the Steelers and Vikings as Madden and Davis get nervous, banter with one another and celebrate their championship with as many f-bombs as possible. The salty language is solely why this movie is rated R and not PG-13. 

As the Raiders celebrate their first title, Madden brings out a birthday cake for Virginia that started out as loving x's and o's but quickly devolved into another diagrammed play. Gillis' McGary is brought into the locker room to celebrate, and a video game creator named Trip Hawkins, who created Electronic Arts and eventually makes the Madden video game, first introduces himself to the head coach somehow at the Super Bowl postgame press conference. John Mulaney played Hawkins yet didn't mention the movie once when he hosted "Saturday Night Live" this past weekend, continuing a theme of Amazon, which produced the movie, not wanting to promote the film too much and backing away from a previously planned wide theatrical release.

Madden and Davis are inseparable even after the championship, yelling plays at each other and rationalizing how Madden hasn't seen his family in months to the point where he forgets how old his two sons are. Madden starts complaining about his stomach pain, which Davis says can be cured with saltines and Tums, specifically the peppermint kind. It turns out to be a stomach ulcer that forces Madden into retirement from the Raiders, but not before several jokes about vomiting and gas. A serious and dramatic biopic, this is not.

Madden is insufferable as a retired stay-at-home dad, going to see Steve Martin's "The Jerk" several times, hanging with McGary and explaining plays out loud to his dog. Davis convinces Madden to take a meeting with CBS for a color commentator job, which Madden reluctantly accepts despite calling their NFL broadcast team "haircuts." The film then successfully chronicles Madden's rise as a household television superstar, introducing his Madden cruiser bus and fear of flying, his catchphrases and commercials for Miller and Tinactin, the Thanksgiving turducken, his love of food and his pioneering use of the telestrator. 

This sets up an absurd and unrealistic scene where Davis and Hawkins are fighting over Madden's future. Davis wants Madden to come back and consult after a terrible 1987 season and Hawkins wants Madden to give over his beloved five-pound playbook to educate the masses for EA. There's a car chase scene and a ridiculous moment where Davis, who moved the Raiders to Los Angeles, tries explaining the rap group NWA to Madden, who questions whether Dr. Dre actually received a medical degree. 

Madden ultimately agrees to put his name and playbook behind EA, he and Davis make the Hall Of Fame — where Madden believes the busts talk to each other at night — and the rest is history. 

While there are a few brief, tender and heartfelt moments, if director David O. Russell wanted the movie to be a serious, award-winning holiday movie, he failed spectacularly. "Madden" doesn't take itself seriously, and neither should you. The movie will be far more enjoyable to watch if football fans first lower their expectations.

item.title: NFL power rankings: Not everybody is sold on the 49ers being No. 1
item.description: A few outlets have the 49ers second and third.
item.content:encoded:
It’s Tuesday, which means we’ll show the NFL power rankings from around the league, and some thoughts about the San Francisco 49ers.

ESPN

Week 10 result: Beat the Cowboys 46-40
Week 10 ranking: 2

Non-QB MVP at midseason: LB Fred Warner

While QB Brock Purdy is a top candidate for league MVP, Warner is making a strong case to be the first linebacker to win Defensive Player of the Year since Luke Kuechly in 2013. Warner’s 88 tackles rank sixth in the NFL. He’s tied for first in forced fumbles (five) to go with a fumble recovery, 0.5 sacks and three pass breakups. He has done all that after returning from a broken and dislocated right ankle injury that cost him most of last season. For a defense on its fifth coordinator in five years, Warner is the constant and one of the primary reasons the Niners are 8-1. — Nick Wagoner

The Athletic

2. San Francisco 49ers (8-1)

Last week: 2

Sunday: Beat Cowboys 46-40

Breakout player: Renardo Green

The third-year cornerback had a tough day on Sunday against George Pickens and company, but he was dealing with a back injury and had already built up plenty of goodwill this year. Green, a second-round pick in 2024, has four interceptions, three more than he had in his first two seasons combined. Rookie running back Kaelon Black has also been a surprise with 356 rushing yards behind Christian McCaffrey.

NFL

Did I expect San Francisco to give up 40 points to the Cowboys? No, I foresaw them surrendering just 20, in fact. Does that concern me much? No, not really. The 49ers won a wild shootout in Arlington by staying true to themselves offensively — crafting a beautiful blend of creative play-calling with artistic improvisation from Brock Purdy to light up Dallas’ beleaguered defense — and they did enough defensively to get the job done. Nick Bosa isn’t quite making the impact I’d hoped to see in his return from injury, but it’s still early in that process and the defense remains a strong group overall. Until proven otherwise, this is the NFL’s best squad.

Bleacher report

2. San Francisco 49ers

Last Week: 2

Week 10 Result: Won at Dallas 46-40

The San Francisco 49ers continue to look like the best team in the NFC, though they did have some hiccups against the Cowboys on Sunday.

Brock Purdy had another MVP-caliber outing, as Christian McCaffrey, Deebo Samuel, and other 49ers playmakers repeatedly knifed through Dallas’ suspect defense. The deadline trade for receiver Keenan Allen paid immediate dividends, and it’s fun to think about how potent the offense could be once Allen is fully integrated into the game plan and Mike Evans is healthy again.

However, San Francisco’s pass rush continues to underwhelm, and its defense struggled overall in Dallas. Next week’s matchup with the Kirk Cousins-led Vikings will be a massive test.

Yahoo Sports

2. San Francisco 49ers (8-1, LW: 2)

The 49ers cooked the Cowboys’ defense, putting up 46 points and 584 yards. Dallas’ defense is dreadful but it’s still hard to pile up close to 600 yards in any NFL game.

The way the 49ers have climbed to the top of the NFL in yards per game is worth studying. Brock Purdy was famously Mr. Irrelevant in the draft and now he’s an MVP candidate. Christian McCaffrey was at a point in which age and touches should have started to chip away at his effectiveness, but he is tied for the NFL lead with 13 total touchdowns. Draft experts laughed at the Kaelon Black pick in the third round; he’s one of the best backup running backs in the league. Deebo Samuel Sr.’s career looked like it might be over after last season, but he has five touchdowns in six games. The 49ers had to give up only a sixth-round draft pick for Keenan Allen in a trade and he had five catches for 61 yards on Sunday.

The conclusion: Kyle Shanahan is your NFL Coach of the Year.

USA TODAY

1. San Francisco 49ers (1): The defensive performance wasn’t all that inspiring Sunday, but the Niners are re-incorporating players on that side of the ball. They’re still not completely whole on offense, either, WRs Mike Evans and De’Zhaun Stribling the most notable absentees right now. But when you’re averaging 9.4 yards per play anyway, then you’re a pretty dangerous operation − maybe a Super one, though the upcoming matchups with Minnesota and Seattle will be much truer litmus tests than Dallas was.

FOX Sports

Super Bowl odds: +500 (tied for the best)

The 49ers put on some offensive show in Dallas, running up 584 yards and scoring six touchdowns against the Cowboys. Then again, given how soft the Dallas defense has been this season, maybe that’s not as impressive as it sounds. Besides, everyone knew the 49ers were explosive on offense. We all just thought they were better on defense. They were torn apart for 343 yards and five touchdown passes by Dak Prescott, who kept getting the Cowboys back into striking distance of a miracle comeback. If Dallas’ defense was even mediocre, with the ability to make just one more stop, the 49ers would have lost.

Next game: vs. Vikings (Sunday, 8:20 p.m. ET)

Stat To Know: The 49ers averaged 9.4 yards per play against the Cowboys, the most by any team in a game over the past two seasons. They also scored three touchdowns of 60-plus yards from scrimmage, tying the most by any team in a game over the past 50 years.

In the past 30 seasons, there have been 20 instances — including historic teams like the 2007 New England Patriots and "The Greatest Show on Turf" St. Lous Rams teams from 2000-2002 — of the preseason Super Bowl favorite having odds of +500 or better entering a season. And those teams have gone 0-for-20 in their journey to win a Super Bowl as short favorites.

The Rams have fallen to 15-1 odds to win the Super Bowl at BetMGM and are only +105 to make the playoffs (-125 to miss).

The Buffalo Bills (8-1 record) and San Francisco 49ers (8-1) have looked like the two best teams on the field and are Super Bowl co-favorites at +500 odds currently, followed by the Chicago Bears (+750) and Jacksonville Jaguars (+750). The Cincinnati Bengals — fresh off a 38-18 dismantling of the Pittsburgh Steelers on national television behind 409 passing yards and four TDs from MVP favorite Joe Burrow — have 10-1 odds, as do Patrick Mahomes' Kansas City Chiefs.

But the two big Super Bowl odds movers this week resulted from one play on Sunday, when Aidan Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye and then Hutchinson proceeded to injure himself on the celebration.

Unfortunately, for the Lions, it's indeed a torn ACL for Hutchinson, which will sideline him for the rest of the season. Detroit, despite a 7-2 record, moved from 18-1 to 20-1 odds to win the Super Bowl (11th-best odds). item.title: 10 Thoughts on the NFL, Week 10: The Kings in the North
item.description: Move aside Mahomes. There’s a new king in town.
item.content:encoded:
1. Take a bow, Joe Burrow. Show me a guy playing the quarterback position better than that guy right now. Sure, it’s nice to be able to throw to Ja’Marr Chase (11 catches for 231 yards), who is right there with Jaxon Smith-Njigba and Justin Jefferson as the very best receivers in football, and Tee Higgins. But if you’re watching these games, you know what you’re seeing: a quarterback operating at a level few have ever reached. The Bengals’ passing offense was so unstoppable that Cincinnati didn’t even have to run the ball. When Burrow can complete 35 of 44 attempts for 409 yards and four touchdowns, why would you? If you’re asking me to pick an MVP through the halfway point of the season, Burrow’s mine.

2. This is the second straight year the NFC North is inarguably the best division in football. What a time to be alive. Every team in the division has at least six wins so far, with three of those teams (Minnesota, Detroit, and Chicago) sitting at 7-2. And every time they play one another, they’re out there throwing absolute haymakers. Even as a Bears homer, it’s hard to definitively say who the best team in this division is because they won’t stop clobbering the rest of the league, and you have no idea what you’re going to get when they play one another. There is a legitimate chance that every team in the NFC North finishes with a winning record, but someone misses the playoffs again. How cruel is that? (As long as it’s not the Bears…)

3. I don’t agree with Dan Orlovsky on much, but I found myself reluctantly nodding to his take about Aidan Hutchinson after the latter suffered a season-ending knee injury celebrating a sack on Drake Maye. Being amped about getting a sack is great and well-earned. Dance. Pump the fist. Do whatever you want. But keep your feet on the ground when you’re doing it. We’ve seen too many LaMarr Houston situations to have our pass-rushers keep going down like this. That’s now Hutchinson’s second major knee injury in three seasons, and it’s going to hurt a Lions team that keeps outperforming expectations.

4. The Chargers’ unlikely quest to go 0-17 is finally over. And they needed all the Ravens’ help to get it done, too. I love me some Zay Flowers, but man…it’s okay to go down or run out of bounds sometimes. These devastating fumbles have to stop. Then again, not unlike the Patriots now that they’ve likely lost Drake Maye for the season, Baltimore is already cooked without Lamar Jackson. Great tank loss for the Ravens, especially considering Jacoby Brissett, who just got there a few hours ago, played pretty well all things considered. 

5. You know what it means that Dak Prescott (343 yards, 5 TDs) had a QBR of 85.2 on Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers, according to ESPN? It means that he played at basically an All-Pro level. That, even though Brock Purdy (389 yards, 3 TDs) also balled out, there’s no reason that the Cowboys should lose a game in which Prescott played that well. But they did. Because the Cowboys are a joke (outside of Prescott). Because their lame-duck coach never deserved to be there in the first place, and their geriatric owner is more concerned with upholding the good ol’ boys club than winning football games. Because Dallas decided not to cover Christian McCaffrey, the literal best skill player on the team, twice and let Deebo Samuel score on the most Pop Warner-esque play of all time. Free Dak.

6. Who would’ve thought that the moment Patrick Mahomes gets a slot receiver worth a damn, he immediately goes off for five touchdown passes? Seriously, keep an eye on that Josh Downs move to Kansas City as the season goes on. For him to net 53 yards and a score off rip says a lot for his talent and what the Chiefs’ receiving pecking order looks like. While Rashee Rice is clearly the top dog, KC has been searching a while for that slot receiver who can make explosive plays and make Mahomes’ life easier. While no one is quite the cheat code Tyreek Hill was, Downs is plenty good enough. Can’t wait to see how that partnership grows as the year progresses. Lord knows the Colts weren’t worth Downs’ time.

7. It might just be because they play in Jacksonville, and too many people are used to them being awful. But boy, are those Jaguars popping right now. If Joe Burrow is the MVP of the league right now, Trevor Lawrence (2,284 yards, 21 TDs, 5 INTs on the season; 352 yards, 3 TDs on Sunday) is on the short list of runners-up. The funny part: as good as they are on offense right now (fourth in points scored), they’re just as scary on defense (second-fewest points allowed). Something tells me this isn’t the year the Jags win it all. But win a playoff game? I can see it.

8. I don’t care what Donte Whitner says: I thought Jameis Winston having fun with his dummy calls was hilarious. At a certain point, when the defense isn’t jumping and the offense clearly isn’t interested in running a play, you know what the score is. If they didn’t jump on the first few honest attempts to draw them offside, they’re not going to jump with three seconds left on the play clock. In the end, it’s a game. Have fun. It’s not his fault the Washington Commanders gave up that game-losing touchdown and JJ McCarthy threw that pick. Be mad at them.

9. Since I mentioned him earlier, I just want to say it once more: JSN is one of the best receivers I’ve ever seen. And I told a lot of people he would be coming out of college, but people just couldn’t let go of his 40 time. Does he look slow out there while he’s ripping off long touchdowns and putting up 79 catches for 1,207 yards through 10 games? Anyone want to tell me why they thought Quentin Johnston was going to have a better career just because he was 6-4 and could run fast in a straight line? And again, he’s doing this with Sam Darnold, Drew Lock, doesn’t matter. Whether he breaks the single-season record for receiving yards or not, he’s the best of his generation. And again, when he’s putting his resume up against those LSU monstrosities Jefferson and Chase, that’s saying a lot.

10. You know what? Let’s make that the question of the week, and it’s actually a great one because all of them have such unique skill sets. Which Big 3 receiver would you take: JSN, Jefferson, or Chase? Personally, I’m going JSN<Chase<Jefferson, with the margins so narrow you have to look into an electron microscope to see the gaps. How about you?

item.title: Cowboys vs. 49ers: The good, the bad, and ugly from Week 10
item.description: The Cowboys bad always seems to overwhelm the good
item.content:encoded:
Although we all had hope the Dallas Cowboys can pull off the upset, losing to the San Francisco 49ers Sunday afternoon was pretty much expected. The 46-40 score suggests it was a shootout, however, the 49ers pretty much controlled the outcome of the game despite the Cowboys best efforts. They made big plays when needed, which ultimately led to their eighth win of the season.     

Despite suffering yet another loss, the Cowboys continued to play hard to the very end, evidenced by the three touchdowns they scored in the fourth quarter alone. A few key stops here and there may have changed the outcome of the game, but overall it was a mixed bag of positives and negatives for the Cowboys in Week 10. Below is the good, bad, and ugly from this matchup.

THE GOOD – WR George Pickens

Shout out to Quinnen Williams for his continued dominant play Sunday afternoon, but this week’s ‘good’ goes to WR George Pickens. He was questionable entering this Week 10 matchup with a hamstring injury against the 49ers, but you couldn’t tell by the way he played.

He was Dak Prescott’s favorite target and the two connected to the tune of 11 catches for 145 yards and three touchdowns. This was the kind of performance we’ve been wanting to see more from No. 3 and hopefully it’s a sign of things to come.

THE BAD – K Brandon Aubrey

Brandon Aubrey’s inconsistency in the kicking game is starting to become an issue. Once considered “Mr. Reliable” has now turned into “Mr. Inconsistent”. Sundays missed extra point was just another example of how much he continues to struggle this year.

He’s still a big weapon just about any team in the league would love to have on their roster, but with the extra-point tries, field goals, or even kickoffs, he’s no longer as dependable. He’s definitely not living up to that big-money contract he signed recently.

THE UGLY – Defensive letdown

Another week, another defensive letdown for the Cowboys. For the past few weeks they seem to play pretty well in the first half, but then completely fall apart after halftime. It was much the same this week against the 49ers.

Dallas’ defense allowed San Francisco to gain 584 total yards Sunday afternoon, the most they ever surrendered at home. They also allowed a multitude of big plays that ultimately secured the victory for the 49ers. Despite some small improvements, this defense is still playing ugly.

item.title: NFC South Week 10 Review: Carolina takes the lead (for now)
item.description: Sure, the Panthers are in the lead, but is that something to be proud of?
item.content:encoded:
The Panthers and Saints faced off for the division lead in what was one of the worst-officiated games this decade, while the Falcons tried to keep pace with the Chiefs. The Buccaneers had the week off, and fans across the league appreciated seeing one less NFC South team play. Here’s the Week 10 NFC South Review.

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6)

Week 10 Result: Bye Week
Week 11 Opponent: Detroit Lions  

The Buccaneers were on the bye, and they desperately needed it. Tampa Bay was hoping to get some good rest, but it appears Baker Mayfield is dealing with a foot injury that’s bad enough that the team felt like it needed to sign Cooper Rush. I had no idea Rush was a podiatrist, but I’m glad he can find work.

Like every team in this division, the Buccaneers are not out of the title race. They’ll need a near-spotless finish to win the division, and they have a tough start on the road in Detroit.

Carolina Panthers (4-5)

Week 10 Result: Panthers 20 – Saints 17
Week 11 Opponent: Baltimore Ravens 

The Cardiac Cats pulled out the win in the final seconds of this division matchup against the Saints. It was an ugly game for the most part; 20 of the 37 total points were scored in the 4th quarter. Chuba Hubbard led the way on the ground, scoring the Panthers two touchdowns of the game.

Young struggled to complete just over 50% of his passes for 200 yards, but he played a turnover-free game, and that’s what it takes to win a slugfest. Carolina sits atop the division and will host the Ravens next week.

New Orleans Saints (3-6)

Week 10 Result: Saints 17 – Panthers 20
Week 11 Opponent: Chicago Bears

The Saints couldn’t build on their Week 9 win and added another L to their record. Kellen Moore’s offense is out of sorts. Tyler Shough finished another game as the team’s leading rusher, with only 25 yards. The Saints defense had one of their better performances of the season but couldn’t stop the Panthers when it counted.

Things could be worse; they could be last in the division, but that’s not a very high bar. There’s no rest for the wicked; the Saints will travel to Chicago to take on the Monster of the Midway.

Atlanta Falcons (3-7)

Week 10 Result: Falcons 13 – Chiefs 35
Week 11 Opponent: Bye Week

The Falcons got torched by Patrick Mahomes and have the longest active losing streak in the division. Michael Penix has been stuck in a rut for weeks, and the team has been unable to get him out of it. The offense can’t stop committing penalties or turning the ball over. The team had 18 last year; they have 19 and counting this season.

The defense is coming apart at the seams and can’t stop the run or the pass right now. The bye week couldn’t have come at a better time, and they’ll need the extra prep because Brian Flores will be waiting for them.

It’s looking more and more like 7 wins will get the job done this year, which means it’s still anyone’s title for the taking. Some teams should probably face the reality that winning the South won’t help their futures, but that wouldn’t be any fun.
