item.title: Week 10 awards from Bengals’ impressive win vs. Steelers
item.description: A lot of Bengals players shined on the primetime stage.
item.content:encoded:
A 38-18 Sunday night win over your biggest rival, a fifth straight victory, and sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Not a bad weekend in the Queen City.

The stars were brilliant, and we’ll honor them. But a win like this also needs the guys who did the dirty work. Here are my nominees for Team MVP and Unsung Hero of the Week.

Team MVP nominees

Joe Burrow, QB. Burrow went 35-of-44 for 409 yards and four touchdowns with no turnovers, a 135.7 passer rating. He had 302 yards and three scores by halftime, before Aaron Rodgers had done much of anything. He’s now the second quarterback in NFL history with four or more total touchdowns in five straight games, joining Peyton Manning, and his 27 touchdown passes lead the league. If this was his MVP audition on national TV, he nailed it.

Ja’Marr Chase, WR. Chase caught 11 of his 14 targets for 231 yards, 146 of them in the first half. That’s the most receiving yards by any player in a game this season and the fourth-most in Bengals history. His 53- and 43-yard catches both set up touchdowns. He didn’t score, but nobody had a bigger impact on the game.

Boye Mafe, DE. Mafe hit Rodgers three times and sacked him once on a third down, pushing his team-leading total to 6.5 sacks. He was a big reason Pittsburgh had four first downs and 40 total yards at halftime.

Unsung Hero of the Week nominees

Demetrius Knight Jr., LB. Knight led the team with eight tackles, six of them solo, plus a pass breakup and a quarterback hit. On a night when the pass rush got the headlines, Knight was the one cleaning up everything underneath and keeping Pittsburgh’s short game in check.

Jordan Battle, S. Battle was second on the team with six tackles. He added a tackle for loss and a pass breakup, and was all over the field in a secondary that held Rodgers to 15-of-29 passing, with both of his touchdowns coming after the game was decided.

Drew Sample, TE. Sample caught three passes for 15 yards, including the 3-yard touchdown that put the Bengals up 10-0, his second career touchdown catch. As usual, much of his value came as a blocker, the kind of work that never shows up in a box score.

Jonathan Allen and Myles Murphy, DL. Each had a sack. Allen’s, like Mafe’s, came on third down and ended a Steelers drive, and Murphy’s brought his season total to 2.5. Neither will make SportsCenter, but those drive-killers are why Pittsburgh couldn’t find any rhythm early.

The offensive line. Burrow was sacked once all night against a Steelers front that usually lives in the backfield. That’s how a quarterback throws for 302 yards in a half. Dalton Risner hurt his left knee during the game, so keep an eye on his status this week.

Your vote

Who’s your Team MVP: Burrow or Chase? And who did the dirty work best on Sunday night? Make your case in the comments!

And Who Dey!

item.title: Whatever Jared Verse is doing is starting to work: Browns defense
item.description: Jared Verse leads the way for the Browns’ defensive front this week.
item.content:encoded:
The Browns were picked apart in the first quarter of the game, and then in the second half, completely shut down the Texans unlike anything I’ve seen. It’s just confusing how this defense can produce such different results at different points of the game. I understand that they make adjustments, but what about the preparation leading into the game?

Below, we analyze the snap counts and stats on defense for the Cleveland Browns’ Week 10 game against the Houston Texans.

Defensive Line

  • Obviously, the headline of this article is over-exaggerating a little bit with respect to Jared Verse. He still didn’t get a sack or tackle, but he registered a quarterback hit. And, a week after saying he saw a team psychiatrist to try figuring out his on-field struggles, he registered his best PFF grade of the season (74.5), which was third best on defense this week. I’ll take it as a positive. There’s also this:
  • Mike Hall played limited snaps this week among the defensive tackles, as Maliek Collins made his return. On a positive note, some of the defensive tackles fared better in their run defense grades from PFF this week.

Linebacker

  • Carson Schwesinger put together another solid performance, making his presence known all over the field, especially in the second half. It didn’t pay off as far as a PFF grade goes, as he graded out to a 49.3, but I can only speculate that he was part of the team’s early struggles that led to a 17-0 deficit.
  • Quincy Williams had a very solid run defense grade by PFF at 88.7.

Cornerback

  • I know C.J. Stroud had some early on-the-money throws, but the play of Denzel Ward and Tyson Campbell really helped turn this game around. They stepped up to the challenge of defending the Texans’ receivers with no help, and had six passes defended combined.
  • Ward received a PFF grade of 74.0, and Campbell a grade of 83.1. Those were the fourth- and top defensive grades on the day.
  • Myles Harden was the victim of an unfortunate pass interference penalty in the second half that shouldn’t have been a penalty. He’s taken on the aggressive attitude of the corners ahead of him and surpassed my expectations.

Safety

  • Getting the start for Ronnie Hickman, Emmanuel McNeil-Warren played every snap and was the Browns’ second-highest graded defender by PFF (77.6). He had 7 tackles, and an interception/return that was taken off the board. The Browns really need to give some consideration to making him a starter, in my opinion, during the bye week.

item.title: Most common players on eliminated teams from Week 10 in Yahoo Fantasy Death leagues — plus FAB waiver wire advice
item.description: Death Leagues have claimed more star players. Fantasy football analyst Scott Pianowski advises you on how to approach the waiver wire in Week 11.
item.content:encoded:
Every week I'll examine the most common NFL players on the teams eliminated in Yahoo Death Leagues, trying to figure out where the puck is headed. I will also offer some FAB advice ($1,000 cap is the Yahoo default), but please remember this area is highly context-sensitive and manager-specific.

Waiver strategy in Death Leagues

The strategy becomes more and more context-dependent as we meander through the late stages of the season. And it's critical that you audit the FAB budgets remaining for your competitors. It's not unlike poker, where a good player is constantly reevaluating the chip dynamics of the table, who's deep and who's thin. Leverage is everything.

In most leagues the waiver wire will be especially rich every week onward, as the cut teams become stronger and stronger. It's also more plausible to find useful players on the wire for nothing, players who would never be free agents in a casual league. Remember, your manager pool keeps shrinking in size.

You always audit every injury closely, but also pay keen attention to bye weeks. There are six teams who won’t be in action for Week 11 — the Packers, Falcons, Browns, Patriots, Seahawks and Rams. This has to be factored into your strategy.

Understanding FAB recommendations

My weekly FAB recommendations will come in three buckets:

Proactive: This means you highly covet this player, perhaps might even need this player. I realize these offers might not win if someone in your league is lighting money on fire, but as described above, that's often a short-sighted mistake in this format.

Reactive: This means you desire the player but the offer has to make sense for your short- or long-term strategy.

Keep Them Honest: This is an offer that is not designed to win, but might surprisingly land a player if your opponents are distracted by other talent available or unexpectedly passive that week. I often compare notes with other experienced Death League players and we're surprised at how often the Keep Them Honest offers actually win (this is also a portable strategy for regular season-long leagues; you never know when strange market behavior will come about).

One last note: Understand that the FAB recommendations are with the assumption that you won't be making offers for every available player.

Week 10's top-10 players on eliminated teams

1. QB Drake Maye, Patriots (35.4%)

A first-quarter ankle injury wrecked Maye’s day and it’s possible the ankle might be broken. It’s common for the Super Bowl-losing team to encounter a season from hell the following year, and that’s what’s befallen Maye and Co. Unless Maye gets a shocking piece of positive news before your offer deadline, it’s best to sit this one out. The Patriots are off in Week 11.

FAB Recommendation:

  • No bid

2. RB Kyren Wiliams, Rams (23.5%)

Williams was outplayed by teammate Blake Corum against Arizona, and Ronnie Rivers picked up the garbage-time carries. Williams and Corum are likely in a 50-50 split at the moment, where the hot hand will determine weekly production. The Rams are one of six teams on bye in Week 11, so Williams doesn’t offer immediate help. Tread carefully.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $120 proactive

  • $50 reactive

  • $20 keep them honest

3. RB Jonathan Taylor, Colts (22.7%)

Although the Colts were open for business at the trade deadline, they ultimately decided to keep Taylor. Rookie RB Seth McGowan is getting more work than expected, and the Indianapolis offense lacks buoyancy, given the poor play of QB Daniel Jones. Taylor remains a good player, but isn’t the earth-moving pick he looked like in August.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $175 proactive

  • $85 reactive

  • $40 keep them honest

4. RB Jaylen Warren, Steelers (22.6%)

The Steelers quickly junked the running game when Sunday night’s game got out of hand in the first half, but at least Warren ducked in five catches. The recent slump of Aaron Rodgers is a major concern, but the Philadelphia defense presents a get-right spot for Warren and the Steelers in Week 11.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $130 proactive

  • $60 reactive

  • $25 keep them honest

5. WR Christian Watson, Packers (22.1%)

The Minnesota blitz packages had a field day against the Packers, taking the deep pass out of circulation. Watson still holds Circle of Trust privileges, but here’s another player who has to deal with a pesky Week 11 bye.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $135 proactive

  • $65 reactive

  • $25 keep them honest

6. TE Brock Bowers, Raiders (21.1%)

An ankle injury held him to 11 snaps against Seattle and it’s possible Bowers will miss additional time. The Raiders also have a Week 13 bye looming. Given the week-by-week gravity of Death Leagues, Bowers is a risky boom/bust candidate for the current waiver run.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $120 proactive

  • $55 reactive

  • $25 keep them honest

7. WR Chris Olave, Saints (21.1%)

He’s stuck on two touchdowns for the year and Jordyn Tyson has quickly moved into a significant role. The Saints also need to do a better job of game planning — somehow this offense has scored just nine points in the first quarter all year. The remaining schedule is mostly favorable, but Olave is probably more of a WR2 than an elite fantasy play.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $115 proactive

  • $50 reactive

  • $18 keep them honest

8. WR Tetairoa McMillan, Panthers (20.4%)

He’s scored just one touchdown over five weeks, and he hasn’t topped 60 yards since Week 6. Bryce Young is essentially a boom-or-bust quarterback and his receivers are along for the bumpy ride. McMillan also has a nasty rest-of-season slate of matchups, probably the hardest in the league.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $110 proactive

  • $45 reactive

  • $12 keep them honest

9. WR Tee Higgins, Bengals (20.3%)

The Steelers played a bunch of zone coverage against the Bengals — unsuccessfully, as it turned out — and that muted Higgins, a notable man-coverage beater. Nonetheless, the Cincinnati offense is humming right now, and Higgins is currently WR7 on the season. A proactive offer is warranted.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $175 proactive

  • $80 reactive

  • $30 keep them honest

10. RB Javonte Williams, Cowboys (19.8%)

He was kept out of the end zone for just the third time this season, though at least he collected 17 touches. Williams is better when the Cowboys face positive game scripts, as he’s not used much in the passing game. His schedule after the Week 14 bye is especially challenging, but Dallas will be favored over Tennessee and Philadelphia the next two weeks. He’s a useful piece, if not a dominant one.

FAB Recommendation:

  • $140 proactive

  • $70 reactive

  • $25 keep them honest

item.title: Dan Campbell delivers epic answer on Lions’ injury frustration
item.description: Detroit Lions Dan Campbell offered a passionate response to a question about injury frustration.
item.content:encoded:
Ask any Detroit Lions fan, and they’ll tell you about the team’s incredibly unlucky streak when it comes to injuries. It’s not just the number of injuries the Lions have endured, but injuries to their star players. Aidan Hutchinson has now suffered two season-ending injuries. Jack Campbell’s neck injury could threaten his career. Brian Branch tore his Achilles last December, Kerby Joseph has been dealing with a knee injury for over a year, and the Lions lost Alim McNeill to an ACL injury shortly after Hutchinson went down in 2024.

As CBS Sports’ Doug Clawson pointed out this week, over the last three years, Hutchinson, McNeill, Joseph, Campbell and Branch have played on the field at the same time for just 3 percent of snaps—and haven’t all played together in over two seasons (38 straight games).

On Tuesday, Lions coach Dan Campbell was asked if he ever feels frustrated for not having all of his defensive weapons at his disposal all at once. A bit perturbed by the question, Campbell offered a passionate response.

“Yeah, well, I think there’s time where if you’re not careful, you lay in bed in night, and you start thinking about all the what-ifs. And at some point, you just become a miserable piece of shit,” Campbell said. “And I’m not going to do it. We’re not doing it. I refuse to look at it that way.

“Does it stink? Yeah, it sure did in the moment. It’s time to move on. We have to. And what has happened with Jack Campbell, and with Hutch now, will not be in vain. We can’t allow it to. They got us to this point, and so what are we going to do about it, man? Are we just going to let it go to waste, or are we going to do something and pick up the slack?”

This reflects the team’s “next man up” mentality Campbell has preached since taking the job in Detroit. It’s what allowed the Lions to persevere when the Lions lost Hutchinson, McNeill, John Cominsky, Malcolm Rodriguez, and Carlton Davis—among others back in 2024. But now Campbell believes they are better prepared to endure the injury turbulence this year.

“We are much better equipped than we were then,” Campbell said. “That’s the reason why we have the depth that we have in that room. We knew that was important. I mean, these are the things you learn over a six-year period; it’s how important depth is. And so, we feel really good about that room.”

item.title: All four NFC South teams are terrible at home, and one will get a home playoff game
item.description: The NFL's playoff seeding procedures guarantee that an NFC South team will host a playoff game.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL's playoff seeding procedures guarantee that an NFC South team will host a playoff game. It may prove to be the easiest place to play that any road playoff team has ever visited.

All four NFC South teams are terrible at home this season: The first-place Panthers are 1-3 at home. The Buccaneers are 1-4. The Saints and Falcons are both 1-5. Add it up, and the four NFC South teams are a combined 4-17 at home.

But someone has to win the NFC South, and that "someone" will be at home during the wild card round of the playoffs, almost certainly playing some second-place team that finished the regular season with a much better record. Most likely, the NFC South winner will be the No. 4 seed, and the second-place finisher in the NFC North will be the No. 5 seed.

Currently, the NFC North features a three-way tie among the Lions, Vikings and Bears at 7-2. For those three teams, coming in second in their division and starting the playoffs on the road against the NFC South winner might actually be a better path to the Super Bowl than winning the division and starting the playoffs at home against a wild card team, likely an NFC North rival or the Rams or Seahawks.

The major prize to earn in the regular season is the No. 1 seed, which comes with a first-round bye and home-field advantage. For an NFC contender that falls short of the No. 1 seed, the best bet might be the No. 5 seed, and an easy place to play in the first round of the playoffs.

item.title: The prediction markets are questioning Mike Vrabel's job security, again
item.description: During the offseason, the leading prediction markets were calling into question the future of Patriots coach Mike Vrabel.
item.content:encoded:
During the offseason, the leading prediction markets were calling into question the future of Patriots coach Mike Vrabel. At one point, Kalshi had his chances of being the head coach as of Week 1 at only 62.2 percent.

Now that the Patriots have suffered a pair of embarrassing losses, the possibility of Vrabel not being the head coach of the Patriots after the season is creeping up again.

On Kalshi's master list of coaches to be fired by March 2027, Vrabel is at nine percent. On Polymarket, the specific question of whether Vrabel will be out by December 31, 2026 currently stands at 13 percent.

Since the regular season doesn't end until January 10, the notion that he's regarded as having a 13-percent chance of being fired by December 31 suggests that, if the date were shifted to Monday, January 11, the number would be higher.

Could it happen, one year after a Super Bowl berth in Vrabel's first season with the team? The chances seem to be much lower than 13 percent, on the surface. However, there's a weird vibe coming from the team right now, as illustrated by some of the things Vrabel said both after Sunday’s 35-10 loss to the Lions and on Monday.

It's fair to ask whether Vrabel has lost his touch. It's fair to wonder whether his offseason entanglement has eroded some of his authority within the locker room.

Coaches routinely rail against distractions. Vrabel created a significant one that crossed over into mainstream news. While plenty of players would likely shrug at the situation, some may see hypocrisy. Some may have become exhausted by the endless questions from family and friends about the situation.

The failure of any team in the NFL bubbles over from a complex cauldron of factors. The players may not be good enough. The preparation may not be effective enough. Bad luck plays a role.

Still, the coach needs to be able to press the buttons of the players in order to get the most out of them. And it doesn't take much to tune someone out — even a football coach.

Those are the critical questions. Has a critical mass of players tuned him out? Are they not listening to him? Are they not responding to him?

Ultimately, that's something for ownership to monitor and to diagnose. While the organizational play was to sharply turn the page and move on from the scandal, that only works if the team wins. With the Patriots at 5-5 — and with the defense surrendering 881 yards in losses to the Packers and Lions and being outgained by Detroit, 494 yards to 151 — it's important to get to the "why?" residing at the center of the "what the f—k?"

The Patriots still have seven games to play. Four of them are against the 8-1 Bills, the 7-2 Vikings, the 7-2 Chiefs, and the 7-2 Broncos. And they may not have Maye for any of them.

The chances of a playoff berth are slipping away. A winning record may not happen, either. When the season ends, the powers-that-be will have to decide whether they believe that things will be any better in 2027.

item.title: NFL Power Rankings for Week 11: How did the Denver Broncos hold up over the bye?
item.description: The Denver Broncos didn’t play last weekend, but a good chunk of prognosticators didn’t move them an inch up or or down in their weekly power rankings. It would seem those writers believe that the bye week shouldn’t change how they ranked those bye teams the week prior. The same cannot be said for all, […]
item.content:encoded:
The Denver Broncos didn’t play last weekend, but a good chunk of prognosticators didn’t move them an inch up or or down in their weekly power rankings.

It would seem those writers believe that the bye week shouldn’t change how they ranked those bye teams the week prior. The same cannot be said for all, though, as the rest moved them down into the bottom half of the Top 10 for having the week off. One even leapfrogged the Kansas City Chiefs over Denver a week removed from losing to Denver. That’s how the cookie crumbles. Until this Broncos’ squad wins a Super Bowl, they will get no respect from media interests outside of Denver itself. I do like the overdog setup.

Here’s how the Broncos are doing in this week’s power rankings around the web:

NBC Sports – 4th

The next time the Chargers play the Broncos, Sean Payton will tell Jim Harbaugh to stick his “loophole” up his poophole.

ESPN – 7th

The Broncos are the league’s foremost escape artists — six of their seven wins have come by one score — so we’re looking for an MVP from the defense who has closed out those contests. Linebacker Alex Singleton leads the league in tackles per game and run stop win rate, but Allen’s down-to-down relentlessness is the tone-setter for the group. He is second in the league in quarterback hits despite a double-team rate of 79.4% on his pass-rush snaps. Allen impacts almost everything happening around him.

Yahoo Sports – 8th

It’s hard to find an advanced metric that indicates the Broncos should be higher than this. They’re 14th in point differential, ninth in DVOA, 15th in net EPA as of last week and also a stunning 30th in yards per game on offense and 27th in yards allowed per game on defense. Their Super Bowl odds are tied for ninth best, for what that’s worth. But here’s why that doesn’t matter: Denver is 7-2 after stacking (close) wins and has the easiest remaining schedule in the NFL, via DVOA, after playing the hardest schedule to this point in the season.

Here’s what Denver has coming up: vs. Raiders, at Steelers, vs. Dolphins, at Jets, at Raiders, vs. Bills, at Patriots, vs. Chargers. That’s two playoff contenders (assuming Drake Maye’s injury sinks the Patriots) of eight remaining games. Like last season, the Broncos could end up with 13 or 14 wins and an army of naysayers wondering how good they really are.

USA Today – 6th

Their schedule, the league’s easiest down the stretch based on their remaining opponents’ collective winning percentage, suggests they should match last year’s 14-3 record.

Fox Sports – 2nd

The Broncos rode a five-game winning streak into the bye week and are holding onto this spot thanks to the way the 49ers had to hang on to beat the Cowboys. It also helps that the 7-2 Broncos have a really easy schedule over the next five weeks, maybe outside of their Black Friday game in Pittsburgh. They’ll get the Raiders twice, the Dolphins and the Jets, which should give them a great chance to pad their record. It could also give QB Bo Nix a chance to finally get on a long-awaited roll.

CBS Sports – 5th

Coming off the bye, they need to get better play in two areas: Passing game and run defense. If they do, they can make a deep playoff run.

NY Times – 3rd

The fourth-round rookie running back had 36 touches for 192 yards of offense in weeks 8 and 9. That ranked 17th in the league in that stretch. For the season, he’s averaging 9.8 yards per reception, and he could have a big day against a middling Raiders defense this weekend.

What do you think of these power rankings? Share in the comments section below!

item.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em, Sit 'Em: RBs in timeshares you can trust in Week 11 lineups
item.description: Fantasy analyst Fred Zinkie highlights some backup RBs who could crack starting lineups in Week 11.
item.content:encoded:
Let's take a look at the backup RBs who have a Yahoo roster rate under 60% and could help fantasy teams to victory in Week 11. Players are ranked in order of their Week 11 appeal, and their current roster rates are listed in parentheses.

1. Kaelon Black, 49ers (39%)

Two things were clear when the 49ers hung 46 points on the Cowboys. First, Christian McCaffrey is at the top of his game and the clear focal point of the offense. Second, even with McCaffrey having a heavy workload, there is still room for Black to have a significant role. The rookie has logged at least 11 carries in each of the past three games and has found the end zone twice during that stretch. While San Francisco is set for a challenging Week 11 showdown with a stifling Vikings defense, there may be no stopping one of the hottest offenses in football. Black is a flex option each week and an RB2 option in a Week 11 schedule that includes six teams on a bye.

2. Kenny Gainwell, Buccaneers (44%)

Gainwell went into the Bucs' bye week on a high note, having averaged 101 yards from scrimmage in the previous three games. The 27-year-old is clearly second fiddle to Bucky Irving, who has been one of the top fantasy assets this season. But there are plenty of carries to go around in Tampa's run-heavy offense that leads the NFL in yards on the ground. They will likely remain conservative with play-calling when they visit the high-octane Lions in Week 11.

3. Seth McGowan, Colts (18%)

Managers who dropped McGowan when Jonathan Taylor remained with the Colts past the trade deadline were surely second-guessing their decision when McGowan tallied 77 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in a Week 10 win over the Dolphins. While facing Miami is one of the easiest matchups, McGowan is far from a one-game wonder, having averaged 5.8 yards on 34 carries over the past four weeks. After trading their top receivers and watching Daniel Jones struggle throughout the season, the Colts could copy teams like the 49ers and Buccaneers by running their offense through multiple RBs.

4. Alvin Kamara, Saints (58%)

The bad news: Kamara touched the ball just five times in a Week 10 loss to the Panthers. The good news: he turned those touches into two touchdowns. The 31-year-old will continue to have a role in the offense, as Travis Etienne Jr. and Audric Estimé did little with their Week 10 opportunities. Kamara is averaging three catches per game, which gives him additional value in PPR leagues for a possible Week 11 shootout in Chicago.

5. Emari Demercado, Texans (1%)

Woody Marks will miss Thursday Night Football after leaving the Week 10 loss to the Browns with a concussion. David Montgomery may be ready to return for a favorable matchup against the Colts, but he hasn't played since Oct. 11 and may not be ready for a heavy workload. The Texans are double-digit favorites against a defense that has been repeatedly burned by opposing RBs, and Houston could spend the fourth quarter grinding out rushing yards to put the game away. Demercado is a candidate to fill that role after tallying 13 carries in the past two weeks. And if Montgomery remains out, Demercado becomes the starter and jumps at least two spots higher on this list.

6. Justice Hill, Ravens (13%)

Derrick Henry may be reaching the end of his illustrious career. The future Hall of Famer averaged 1.0 yards per carry against a mediocre Chargers defense in Week 10, which was the fourth time in the past five weeks that his average per carry fell below 3.5. Hill has managed to break a couple long runs this season and is averaging 6.8 yards per carry. He has also caught at least three passes in each of his past five games, including a five-catch game in Week 10. Hill should remain involved in Week 11, when the Ravens face a Panthers defense that has allowed the third-most fantasy points per game to RBs.

7. Mike Washington Jr., Raiders (49%)

Although he wasn't especially effective, Washington led the Raiders with 23 rushing yards in a Week 10 loss to the Seahawks. Starter Ashton Jeanty once again dominated receiving targets, while Washington has led the team in rushing yards in four of their past five games, and his 3.9 yards per carry this season tops Jeanty's 3.2 mark. Washington should earn 8-10 carries but a lack of passing-game involvement gives him a low ceiling for a challenging Week 11 matchup in Denver.

8. Tank Bigsby, Eagles (9%)

Anyone who has watched Saquon Barkley in recent weeks knows that he is not fully healthy. The generational talent lacks his usually explosive burst, and it doesn't help that the Eagles are missing multiple starters while sitting at 2-7. Bigsby is expected to return from injured reserve for a Week 11 matchup against the Steelers, and he should immediately slot ahead of Elijah Mitchell on the depth chart. Bigsby could get 5-10 carries in that game and is worth stashing in the event that the Eagles eventually shut Barkley down for their meaningless late-season games.

9. Chris Rodriguez Jr., Jaguars (37%)

Bhayshul Tuten was used heavily in a 40-point explosion in Week 10, carrying the ball 26 times and catching three passes. Rodriguez had an especially quiet day, with five yards on four carries. Truthfully, if there were fewer than six teams on a bye in Week 11, he would likely fall off this list. But with a dearth of alternatives, he's a TD-dependent flex option in deep leagues for a challenging matchup against a Giants defense that has allowed the seventh-fewest fantasy points per game to RBs.

10. Ray Davis, Bills (4%)

Davis has had almost no impact on Buffalo's offense this season, totaling just 92 total yards over nine games played. Most weeks, Ty Johnson would be the Bills backup who could dent deep-league rosters, as he has caught 18 passes for 214 yards. But the Bills are massive favorites for a Week 11 home game against the 1-8 Dolphins, with the point spread sitting around 16-17 points. If the team builds a massive lead, Davis is the most likely candidate to receive plenty of second-half carries.

10 Backup RBs to Stash

The players listed below are unlikely to provide significant assistance in Week 10 but are an injury away from having significant value.

  • 1. Kaleb Johnson, Packers (bye week)

  • 2. Sione Vaki, Lions

  • 3. Samaje Perine, Bengals

  • 4. Bam Knight, Cardinals

  • 5. Keaton Mitchell, Chargers

  • 6. Dylan Sampson, Browns (bye week)

  • 7. Corey Kiner, Patriots

  • 8. Tyjae Spears, Titans

  • 9. Kimani Vidal, Chargers

  • 10. Austin Ekeler, Commanders

Injured Backups to Stash

  • RJ Harvey, Broncos

  • Jonathon Brooks, Panthers

  • Tyler Goodson, Cowboys

  • Tyrone Tracy Jr., Giants

  • Brian Robinson Jr., Falcons

item.title: Fernando Mendoza era off and running
item.description: How did rookie class fare in Week 10?
item.content:encoded:
Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a home 21-13 loss to the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday and what to look for Sunday at the Denver Broncos.

Fernando Mendoza:
The No. 1 overall pick made his starting debut in Week 10. He started great, scoring a touchdown himself on the ground on the Raiders’ first drive and the Raiders scored a field goal on his second drive. It got rough after that as Seattle adjusted. Mendoza was sacked six times. He completed 17 of 29 passes for 143 yards. He did have some moments where he showed his poise and accuracy. In the end, it was a rough day for Mendoza, but he showed the game wasn’t too big for him and he will continue to grow.

Treydan Stukes:

The Raiders’ second-round pick played every defensive snap as usual.

Trey Zuhn:

The third-round pick made his third straight start and he looks entrenched as a starter.

Jermod McCoy:

The fourth-round pick played just nine defensive snaps after playing extensively in the previous two games. He did spell Eric Stokes when he was briefly injured.

Mike Washington:

The fourth-round pick played 29 percent in Week 10 after he played 34 percent of the snaps in Week 9 after playing 60 percent in Week 8. He had eight carries for 23 yards against the Seahawks. He is averaging 3.8 yards a carry.

Dalton Johnson:

The fifth-round pick safety was inactive for the ninth time in 10 games.

Zeke Masses:

The fifth-round pick started fir the fifth time, but he played just 40 percent of the snaps and struggled at times. It will be interesting to see how much he plays at Denver.

Malik Benson:

The sixth-round pick was a healthy scratch for the third straight game.

item.title: Jerry Jones says Cowboys are discussing defensive coordinator Christian Parker's role after Brian Schottenheimer declines to support him
item.description: Brian Schottenheimer said they are taking a "deep dive" at everything amid their defensive woes.
item.content:encoded:
Brian Schottenheimer, at least publicly, isn't backing his defensive coordinator.

The Cowboys head coach didn't directly support defensive coordinator Christian Parker on Monday, one day after a brutal showing from the Dallas defense in its 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers.

Instead, he said everything is still under review.

"We're still working through the process, talking to the guys is the first step," Schottenheimer said, via The Dallas Morning News. "At the end of the day, there's a lot of things that we need to clean up as a football team. That starts with me."

The 49ers racked up 584 yards of offense and averaged 9.4 yards per play in the win on Sunday. They ran for 214 yards, too, and put up 29 points and 340 yards in the second half alone. It was simply an offensive clinic that the Cowboys couldn't stop time and time again. 

The 584 yards that Dallas allowed was the most they've allowed in a home game in franchise history.

Schottenheimer said after the game that he thought the defense was "unacceptable," and he called the tackling "atrocious."

"At the end of the day, we tackled like s**t in the second half," he said.

Dallas' defensive issues are nothing new. They've been a problem all season, and it's led to louder and louder calls to make a change at defensive coordinator. Parker is in his first season in the role, which also marks his first coordinator job in the NFL. 

Though he declined to support Parker again on Monday, Schottenheimer did not say he was going to make a change.

"I'm not saying that," he said. "I'm saying we're still in the process of going through all the film and evaluation of where we stand today."

Perhaps more importantly, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones did back Parker on Sunday afternoon.

"Again, it's what it is," Jones said postgame. "He's a young coach in his first year of coordinating and calling the plays. So you have to say that you would hope you could win games like the last that we've lost.

"I'll weigh his early times. I've been with teams that had some pretty good coordinators on defense that ended up winning Super Bowls."

But instead of following Jones' lead, Schottenheimer said simply that they are "taking a deep dive" and "looking at everything."

During his weekly appearance on 105.3 The Fan in Dallas, all Jones would say is that Parker's position has come up.

"We're talking about that, but I'm not going to talk about it here," Jones said. "But we are talking about those things."

Jerry Jones on @1053SS, @rjchoppy and @BobbyBeltTX on Christian Parker's future:

"We're talking about that, but I’m not going to talk about that here. But we are talking about those things.” pic.twitter.com/Ovoh1IUXSl

— 105.3 The FAN (@1053thefan) November 17, 2026

The Cowboys are still in the playoff hunt despite their 4-6 record, thanks to a rough NFC East. They are only two games behind the New York Giants. They'll take on the Tennessee Titans next weekend. But the Cowboys haven't won a Super Bowl since the 1995 season, and this team doesn't appear capable of ending that streak. 

The frustration that fans feel, vice president Stephen Jones said, is being felt internally, too.

"I certainly understand their frustration because there's no doubt that we're frustrated," the younger Jones said on 105.3 The Fan. "We feel like the way we're playing ball right now is unacceptable. Our fans certainly deserve better."

Whether the outcry and issues on defense result in a change at defensive coordinator before the end of the season, however, is still anybody's guess.

item.title: Ravens Snap Count Analysis, Week 10: Run defense and run offense crater in fifth straight loss
item.description: Breaking down offensive and defensive snap counts from the Ravens’ Week 8 loss to the Buffalo Bills
item.content:encoded:
Offense
  • QB: Jacoby Brissett 69
  • RB: Derrick Henry 38, Justice Hill 33
  • WR: Rashod Bateman 63, Zay Flowers 61, Ja’Kobi Lane 44, Chris Moore 6, Devontez Walker 3, LaJohntay Wester 1
  • TE: Mark Andrews 40, Matthew Hibner 22, Nick Vannett 14, Josh Cuevas 11
  • OL: Ronnie Stanley 69, John Simpson 69, Cam Jurgens 69, Roger Rosengarten 69, Vega Ioane 36, Chuma Edoga 33, Carson Vinson 9

Jacoby Brissett’s debut with the Ravens saw him play every offensive snap (69). He appeared to suffer a knee injury in the first quarter but shook it off and missed no plays. The entire starting offensive line also went the distance with the exception of Vega Ioane, who departed after 36 snaps due to a shoulder injury. Practice squad call-up Chuma Edoga replaced him at right guard for the final 33 offensive plays.

The running back split saw Derrick Henry play 38 snaps to Justice Hill’s 33 snaps. Henry was rendered ineffective by the Los Angeles Chargers’ defensive front, gaining just 10 rushing yards on 10 carries. The Ravens once again struggled to get any push in the running game and open up lanes.

Mark Andrews had his best game of the season in a position-high 40 snaps, catching eight passes for 82 receiving yards — both of which led the team. Despite playing only 11 snaps, Josh Cuevas was the only other tight end to catch a pass. He had three receptions for 37 yards. Matthew Hibner and Nick Vannett were not targeted.

It was a three-man show at wide receiver, where Rashod Bateman surprisingly out-snapped Zay Flowers slightly (63 to 61). Flowers had six receptions for 74 yards but lost a crucial fumble late in the fourth quarter with the Ravens threatening to tie the game or take the lead. Bateman caught three passes for 42 yards. Ja’Kobi Lane continues to operate as the clear No. 3 wideout and saw the most targets on the team (11). He caught three balls for 61 yards, but dropped a costly third-down pass that would have set up a first-and-goal.

Defense
  • DL: Travis Jones 43, Broderick Washington 32, Calais Campbell 28, Nnamdi Madubuike 28, John Jenkins 10
  • EDGE: Mike Green 45, Trey Hendrickson 41, Zion young 15, Ethan Burke 13
  • ILB: Roquan Smith 57, Trenton Simpson 47, Teddye Buchanan 5
  • CB: Nate Wiggins 53, Marlon Humphrey 42, Keyon Martin 18, Chidobe Awuzie 16, T.J. Tampa 3
  • S: Kyle Hamilton 56, Malaki Starks 54, K’Von Wallace 11, Keondre Jackson 10

Nnamdi Madubuike left the game early with a hamstring injury after 28 snaps, which opened the door for Broderick Washington to play elevated snaps (32). Travis Jones led all defensive linemen with 43 snaps and Calais Campbell had two quarterback hits in his 28 snaps. The Ravens struggled to defend the run, as they allowed 160 rushing yards and the Chargers averaged 4.7 yards per carry with two touchdowns.

On the edge, Mike Green’s 45 snaps saw him wreak havoc with four solo tackles, two sacks, two tackles for loss and three quarterback hits. Green has been the team’s most effective sack-getter this season. Trey Hendrickson played 41 snaps but had just one tackle with no sacks or quarterback hits. Zion Young and Ethan Burke each saw a big reduction in playing time.

Roquan Smith was the lone defender to play 100% of snaps. Trenton Simpson was on the field for all but 10 plays alongside him, recording eight tackles, two quarterback hits and a tackle for loss. Teddye Buchanan’s playing time continue to be minimal, as he played just five snaps. Kyle Hamilton left the field for one play to be checked for a concussion but quickly returned. Malaki Starks played 54 snaps, while the backup safeties combined to take on 21 snaps.

At cornerback, Marlon Humphrey was on the sidelines at times but did not see a huge reduction in playing time as he finished with 42 snaps. Nate Wiggins was nearly on the field for every down, Chidobe Awuzie only played 16 snaps on the outside. T.J. Tampa reverted back to a minimal defensive role (three snaps) and Keyon Martin’s 18 snaps were the third most at the position.

item.title: Enemy Reaction 2026: Las Vegas Raiders fans lose it watching Seahawks game!
item.description: Relive the Seahawks’ win over the Raiders through Enemy Reaction!
item.content:encoded:
The Seattle Seahawks spent a weekend in Las Vegas and left as a winner. So much for “the house always wins” when you play the Las Vegas Raiders, I suppose. Klint Kubiak’s first game against Mike Macdonald started well and fizzled out hard, with rookie QB Fernando Mendoza having his “Welcome to the NFL” moment after an early 10-7 lead. Seattle rode some explosive pass plays and dominant defense to get a 21-13 win that wasn’t as close as the score indicated.

Enemy Reaction is back! We gave the Arizona Cardinals a reprieve because, well, they’re the Cardinals. The Raiders? Not so much, and I haven’t done a Raiders Enemy Reaction in eight years. Comments from the Raiders game threads are courtesy of Silver and Black Pride.

Drew Lock fumbles on second play, Raiders recover (0-0)

Fernando Mendoza runs in the QB draw for his first NFL touchdown (7-0 LV)

JSN touchdown wiped out due to offensive PI (7-0 LV)

Ball don’t lie! Drew Lock scrambles, finds Cooper Kupp for six! (7-7)

Devon Witherspoon welcomes Fernando Mendoza to the NFL (10-7 LV)

Jadarian Price gives the Seahawks the lead with his first NFL touchdown! (14-10 SEA)

Drew Lock to JSN for a 71-yard touchdown! (21-10 SEA)

A mix-up results in a Drew Lock fumble, Raiders recover (21-10 SEA)

Jason Myers misses field goal (21-10 SEA)

Tory Horton saves the ball, takes away the Raiders’ two-minute warning (21-13 SEA)

Drew Lock calls game, Seahawks win! (21-13 SEA FINAL)

Post-game recap: The good and bad from Fernando Mendoza’s debut (Warren Mitchell, Raiders Beat)

Mendoza’s arm talent is elite

He didn’t beat the Seahawks downfield, but Mendoza’s release is much quicker than Cousins’ release and going forward he is going to be able to get passes into tight windows that Cousins cannot.

Mendoza was not always on the same page with his receivers, but that probably had a lot to do with his lack of first-team reps.

Contrary to reports, the CBS broadcast said Mendoza didn’t get many first-team reps before last week, and the majority of the first-team reps he received before last week were running plays.

Now the bad…

Mendoza held onto the ball too long

He had a tendency to hold on to the ball too long in college and it happened a few times on Sunday, especially in the second half.

In the first half, Mendoza threw the ball away under pressure. In the second half, he held on to the ball and took unnecessary sacks.

The receivers played a role in some of the sacks (they couldn’t create separation), but Mendoza still has to avoid negative plays when no one is open.

Post-game video: Grading Fernando Mendoza’s debut and ripping the Raiders defense (JT The Brick)

Enemy Preaction: San Francisco 49ers (sure, and the Dallas Cowboys too!)

We can have a little relaxation (but only a little) for Week 11, as the Seahawks have a bye week and even immediate playoff rivals like the Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers also have Week 11 off. We’ll presumably all be big Minnesota Vikings fans when they play the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City, because that’s the one possible path for Seattle to get back into the NFC West race.

Rest up, heal up, and let’s see the Seahawks have another classic second-half surge like we saw last year, and certainly in a few of the Pete Carroll years!

Thanks for reading and go ‘Hawks!
